## ADR-017: Order Resend Delivery — same-game package swap + live price reconciliation (design only, not yet built)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-07-27 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time, informed by direct review of the legacy KeroxShop admin's own "Resend Delivery" modal and Order Details screen — real screenshots, not recalled from memory — per this project's long-standing rule that the legacy system is UI/UX reference only, never a source of product facts, [`legacy-reference-notes.md`](./legacy-reference-notes.md))

**Context:** ORD-7's currently-shipped `retryDelivery()` (`OrderController::retryDelivery()` → `FulfillOrderJob` → `OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()`) is a purely **idempotent resend**: it re-submits the exact same `supplier_product_ref`/`player_id`/`server_id` already snapshotted on the `Order` row, reusing the same `reference_number` (ORD-8, unchanged), and only ever runs while `delivery_status=failed`. It cannot change what's being delivered. A founder audit of the legacy KeroxShop admin's own Resend Delivery flow surfaced a materially richer feature: the admin can swap to a **different package**, sees a live price comparison against what the customer actually paid, re-validates the Player ID before resending, and the order detail page keeps a **full history** of every attempt (not just the latest). This ADR designs that richer flow for this codebase — grilled one decision at a time, since it touches money/ledger correctness (`ADR-002`), not just UI.

**Decision (per sub-area, each grilled with the founder one at a time before being accepted):**

1. **Scope: same-game package swap only.** Admin may resend against a *different* `Package`, but only one belonging to the **same `Game`** as the original order. Swapping the game itself is explicitly **deferred, not abandoned** (see decision #9) — this phase ships the lower-risk half first.
2. **Checkout snapshot stays immutable — ORD-9 is unchanged.** `Order.cost_price`/`reseller_cost_price`/`selling_price`/`final_amount`/`transaction_fee` are the historical record of what the customer was actually charged at checkout time and are **never rewritten** by a resend. A resend is a new financial event layered on top of that record, not a retroactive edit of it.
3. **Live price is a reconciliation check, not a replacement for the snapshot.** At resend time, the selected package's *current* `cost_price`/`reseller_cost_price` (already kept live by Price Sync's Price Propagation, `ADR-015`) is compared against the original order's snapshotted values, purely to answer "has this gotten more/less expensive since checkout." The platform always **absorbs** the difference in either direction — never re-charges the customer, never blocks a resend over a price increase — but "absorb" must never mean "don't record." Per the founder: failing to record a 1-sen loss is worse than the loss itself.
4. **New audit table, `order_resend_attempts` — one row per resend attempt**, mirroring this codebase's existing `price_change_logs`/`deactivation_logs` discipline (insert-only, no `updated_at`): `order_id` (cascade), `package_id` (the package actually used *this* attempt — may differ from `Order.package_id`), `cost_price_sen`/`reseller_cost_price_sen` (live values read at attempt time), `price_diff_sen` (this attempt's cost vs. the order's original snapshot), `outcome` (success/failed), `supplier_response` (raw JSON), `note` (nullable, admin's own free-text — matches the legacy modal's "Note (Optional)" field), `triggered_by` (admin, nullable). This is what the Admin Orders detail page renders as a "Delivery Logs" history table — today's schema only ever has `Order.supplier_response`, overwritten on every attempt, so no history survives past the latest try.
5. **`final_amount`/`selling_price`/`transaction_fee` stay immutable — never touched by a resend, no exception.** These are the customer-facing record of what was actually charged, and are also the source of truth for total-sales analytics/reporting — a resend, or any package swap, must never retroactively change what a sales report says the customer paid. **`platform_profit`/`reseller_profit`, by contrast, are updated at the moment delivery finally succeeds** (whichever attempt that is — original or resent) to mirror whatever was actually credited to the ledger for that order. Reasoning: `creditProfit()` only ever fires once, on the attempt that actually succeeds (no earlier attempt ever credits the ledger — confirmed in `OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()`), so there's no double-credit risk either way — but if these two fields stayed frozen at the checkout-time estimate while a resend's `LedgerEntry` credits a *different*, recomputed figure, `Order` would permanently disagree with its own ledger entry for the same order. These fields exist to mirror the ledger, not to preserve a pre-delivery estimate — same discipline as Price Propagation updating `Package.cost_price` to live truth, applied here to `Order`'s own profit fields, with `order_resend_attempts` (#4) as the audit trail for every intermediate figure along the way. Confirmed with the founder, 2026-07-27: total-sales analytics must key off the immutable customer-charged fields above, never off profit, which is exactly why this split is safe.
6. **Player-ID re-validation is conditional on `Game.player_validator_enabled`** (the toggle already shipped in `/admin/games`, `ADR-005`'s newest addendum). If enabled, the resend flow must run a validate-ID step (reusing the existing `PlayerValidationController`/`PlayerValidator` chain) before the resend button is actionable. If the game has no validation configured, the resend proceeds directly — no new schema, this reuses an existing mechanism end to end.
7. **Supplier reference handling — no change from today's already-correct behavior.** `Order.reference_number` (ours) is reused unchanged across every resend attempt (ORD-8, unaffected by this ADR). `Order.supplier_ref` (the supplier's own returned ID) already gets overwritten to the latest value on a successful `fulfill()` call — confirmed in the current `OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()` implementation, nothing to build here.
8. **No new `DeliveryStatus` value for a supplier-side post-success reversal ("refunded by supplier").** `delivery_status` stays binary (delivered/failed) — a supplier that reports a refund/reversal reason does so inside its own raw response body, which this codebase already stores verbatim (`Order.supplier_response`). Any "refunded (Supplier)" badge is purely a UI-level read of that existing raw field when a supplier happens to populate it — some suppliers give a reason, some don't (a bare "failed" the admin must manually confirm with the supplier directly), and that variability is inherent to the data, not something to model as a state machine.
9. **Cross-game package swap — explicitly deferred, not abandoned.** The legacy system itself never built this either; it was previously deprioritized on the reasoning that Voucher issuance already lets a customer choose a different game themselves, so an admin-side cross-game swap was judged redundant complexity for the same outcome. The founder still wants it eventually. Tracked for its own dedicated future grill session, which must cover at minimum: (a) Player-ID re-validation is **not optional** when the target game differs from the original — a validated ID for one game carries zero meaning for another, this is a different player account, not just a different SKU; (b) a package-discovery/equivalence UX across unrelated games (no schema for this exists today); (c) whether Voucher's existing self-service path still makes this not worth the complexity, or whether the founder's motivation (reducing customer friction/drop-off after a failure) justifies it anyway.

**Rationale:** Every sub-area above changes `OrderFulfillmentService`'s *implementation* around a resend, not the money-computation contracts `PricingService`/`CheckoutTotalService` already own — the same "deepen the module, don't reshape the seam" discipline this codebase has followed since `ADR-001`/`ADR-006`/`ADR-014`. Decision #3's "always absorb, always record" directly extends `ADR-002`'s ledger philosophy (full audit trail over a clean number) into a new scenario the ledger design didn't originally anticipate.

**Consequence to track:** this ADR records *design intent only* — no code exists yet, matching this project's own established practice of designing and grilling before building (`ADR-013`/`ADR-015`/`ADR-016`). All 9 decisions above are founder-confirmed, including #5's profit-field-vs-customer-charged-field split. Decision #9 (cross-game) is out of scope for whatever ships from this ADR — do not build it opportunistically alongside decisions #1–8 just because the code is nearby. Update `prd.md` §14/§15 once this actually ships.

**Addendum, 2026-07-27 (build session) — decisions #1–8 shipped, #9 still deferred:** `order_resend_attempts` (decision #4) now exists, same insert-audit discipline as `price_change_logs`/`deactivation_logs`. `OrderResendService` (`app/Services/Fulfillment/`) enforces, in order: the order is currently `delivery_status=failed` (decision #8's own state machine, unchanged — resend doesn't loosen the guard `retryDelivery()` already had), the target `Package.game_id` matches the order's own `game_id` and is active (decision #1), and — only when `Game.player_validator_enabled` and a profile is assigned — a recent `player_validations` row exists for the order's own player_id/server_id (decision #6, reusing `CheckoutController::assertPlayerIdIsValidated()`'s exact data-tuple-match discipline, not a new mechanism). `OrderController::resend()` pre-checks the same two guards synchronously for fast admin feedback, then dispatches `ResendOrderDeliveryJob` (ADR-014's async discipline — the admin panel never blocks on a live Gamevion call); the job re-derives live package values at actual attempt time and delegates to `OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()` unchanged.

One concrete formula decision this ADR's own text left open, resolved during implementation: decision #5 says platform_profit/reseller_profit are "recomputed... to mirror whatever was actually credited," but doesn't specify the formula. Implemented by reusing `PricingService::calculate()` — the exact same function `CheckoutService::initiate()` already calls — against the *live* `cost_price`/`reseller_cost_price` of the package actually being resent, at the order's original `reseller_markup_pct`. This mirrors decision #5's own analogy ("same discipline as Price Propagation... applied here") rather than inventing a bespoke absorption formula: `Order.cost_price`/`reseller_cost_price`/`selling_price`/`final_amount`/`transaction_fee` stay exactly as decision #2 requires (never touched), while `platform_profit`/`reseller_profit` are set to this recomputed breakdown *before* `fulfill()` runs, so `creditProfit()`'s existing "fires exactly once, on success" guarantee credits the ledger with these figures — and if the attempt fails, nothing was credited, matching the checkout-time flow's own existing "stored figure is an estimate until delivery actually succeeds" behavior (not a new invariant introduced by this ADR).

Admin UI: `/admin/orders`' existing order-detail view (not a separate route) gained a "Resend Delivery…" button (gated on `delivery_status=failed`, matching the backend exactly) opening a modal — same-game active-package picker with a live cost-price reconciliation preview, an inline "Verify Player ID" step that only renders when the game requires it, and an optional note — plus a "Delivery Logs" table below the existing detail cards rendering every `order_resend_attempts` row, most recent first. 21 new backend tests (`OrderResendServiceTest` 12, `ResendOrderDeliveryJobTest` 4, `OrderControllerTest` +5 resend cases); full suite 396, all green. `npx tsc --noEmit`/`next build`/`eslint` all clean. Verified live against a real running `php artisan serve` + real Sanctum token: `GET /api/orders/{id}` returns the new `resend_attempts` relation, `POST .../resend` correctly 422s a cross-game package and 200s + queues a same-game one. **Not verified live**: an actual queued `ResendOrderDeliveryJob` run against the real Gamevion adapter — deliberately not attempted, since `GAMEVION_SANDBOX`'s real value wasn't checked first and ADR-006's own sandbox `500` limitation (or worse, an accidental real production call) makes that an action to take deliberately, not as a side effect of testing this feature. Decision #9 (cross-game swap) remains explicitly out of scope, not built.

**Addendum, 2026-07-27 (same session) — UI merged, one button instead of two:** first cut shipped "Resend Delivery…" as a *second* button next to ORD-7's original "Retry Delivery" (both gated on `delivery_status=failed`). Founder feedback: two buttons for "fix a failed delivery" was more confusing than useful — an admin shouldn't have to know in advance whether they want the plain-retry or package-swap variant before clicking. Consolidated to a single "Resend Delivery…" button whose modal **defaults the package picker to the order's own package** — submitting with no change reproduces the old "Retry Delivery" behavior exactly (the submit button itself even relabels to "Retry Delivery" when the selection is unchanged, "Resend Delivery" when it differs), routed entirely through the one resend flow (`OrderResendService`/`ResendOrderDeliveryJob`/`POST .../resend`) rather than two separate code paths. If the order's original package was deactivated since it failed (decision #1's own active-package guard would reject resubmitting to it), the modal leaves the picker empty and shows an explicit "original package no longer active — choose a replacement" notice instead of silently failing. The plain `POST /api/orders/{order}/retry-delivery` endpoint (ADR-014, `OrderController::retryDelivery()`) is unchanged and still exists on the backend — no reason to remove a working, tested primitive — it's simply no longer called from this UI; `admin/src/lib/orders.ts`'s `retryOrderDelivery()` helper was removed as genuinely dead frontend code once nothing called it. No backend logic changed, so no test/behavior impact beyond the admin UI itself.

## ADR-018: Sandbox Test Orders — a middleware-only tool for exercising the real Order lifecycle without touching real data or real money

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-07-27 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time, same session as ADR-017's build; explicit founder instruction: record the full plan here for review before writing any code)

**Context:** Testing an order-lifecycle feature (Resend Delivery, order detail, Delivery Logs) today means either driving the real storefront through a real Xendit test-mode checkout every time, or creating an `Order` row by hand via `tinker` against `/admin/orders` and manually deleting it from the DB afterward once done — the exact workflow used to verify ADR-017 live this session. Founder flagged this as untenable for repeated testing and pointed to a real reference: the legacy KeroxShop admin's own middleware "Orders" page (`manage.keroxshop.com`, screenshot reviewed live) has a "Create Test Order" form and a "Test Orders" results table — but by the founder's own account, despite being labeled "test," that table is **not actually isolated** from real order data. That's the specific mistake this ADR exists to not repeat: the goal is a real, working sandbox — not a "test" label that doesn't actually mean anything downstream.

Also confirmed live (not assumed) before deciding the payment approach: fetched `docs.xendit.co/apidocs/simulate-payment-test-mode` directly — Xendit's Payment Request API v3 has no separate test host (test vs. live is purely which secret key is used) and ships an official `POST /v3/payment_requests/{id}/simulate` test-only endpoint that pushes a payment toward `SUCCEEDED` via the normal webhook. Real and useful for testing the *payment* pipeline specifically — but that pipeline is already proven live (`ADR-001`, the Payment Methods "Test" action) and is not what this sandbox exists to exercise, which is why decision #3 below skips it entirely rather than building against it.

**Decision (per sub-area, each grilled with the founder one at a time before being accepted):**

1. **Storage: reuse the real `orders` table, one new `orders.is_test` boolean column (default `false`) — not a parallel schema.** A sandbox order is a real `Order` row. This is what lets `PricingService`, `OrderResendService`, `OrderFulfillmentService`'s status-transition logic, `order_resend_attempts`, and every existing money/delivery code path run **completely unchanged** against it — the only thing that makes it "sandbox" is (a) which controller/page can reach it and (b) two narrow, explicit safety guards (decisions #5/#6). This directly targets the legacy system's actual flaw: a "test" label is worthless unless something concrete enforces exclusion downstream — here that enforcement is a hard, unconditional scope, not a flag anyone has to remember to check.
2. **UI/API placement: fully separate from `/admin/orders`, not a filter/tab inside it.** New page, `/middleware/sandbox` (naming TBD at build time), backed by a new, dedicated `Middleware\SandboxOrderController` (`index`/`store`/`show`/`resend`/`destroy`) whose every query is unconditionally scoped to `is_test = true`. `Admin\OrderController::index()`/`show()` gain a **permanent, unconditional** `where('is_test', false)` — not an admin-toggleable filter — so the real operational queue can never show sandbox data regardless of future changes to that page. Founder's own reasoning: `/admin/orders` is a money-critical tool that must be 100% trustworthy at a glance (e.g. the "Need Action" count); mixing in sandbox data — even filtered, even badged — adds a class of mistake (a filter bug, a future teammate not knowing a toggle exists) that's cheaper to eliminate structurally than to guard against per-screen. This also matches this project's own existing `/middleware` vs `/admin` split (supplier-integration/dev tooling vs. running-the-shop) — DEV-1/DEV-2's raw supplier tester already lives in `/middleware` for the same reason.
3. **Creation skips Xendit entirely — `payment_status` is set to `paid` immediately, no payment call of any kind.** Admin picks a real `Game`/`Package` from our own catalog (via the existing `GET /api/games`/`GET /api/games/{game}/packages` admin endpoints — not raw supplier fields typed by hand, unlike legacy's page) so `PricingService` computes real, consistent money figures. Player ID/Server ID and customer email/name are editable but default to fixed sandbox placeholders. Rejected alternative: Xendit's own `/simulate` endpoint (confirmed to exist, see Context) — not used, since it would add an async payment_status=pending wait for a pipeline already proven live elsewhere, for zero benefit to what this tool actually needs to prove.
4. **Sandbox orders are created directly at `delivery_status = failed`** (skipping `not_started`/`processing`) — framed as "pretend a first delivery attempt already happened and failed." This is deliberate, not an oversight: it's the exact state `OrderResendService`'s existing guard requires before a resend is actionable, so a freshly created sandbox order is immediately usable with the real, unmodified Resend Delivery UI — no separate "first delivery" affordance needs to be built.
5. **Delivery never calls the real `GamevionAdapter` — a new `FakeSupplierAdapter` (`App\Services\Supplier\`, implements the existing `SupplierAdapter` interface) is used instead, swapped in by construction, not by branching inside the fulfillment/resend services.** `Middleware\SandboxOrderController::resend()` builds its own `OrderResendService`/`OrderFulfillmentService` instance directly (constructor-injecting `FakeSupplierAdapter`) rather than resolving `SupplierAdapter` through the container's default binding (which stays `GamevionAdapter`, untouched, for the real `Admin\OrderController` path) — the same substitution the Adapter pattern (`ADR-006`) exists to make cheap. Runs **synchronously, inline, no queue dispatch** — `ResendOrderDeliveryJob`/`FulfillOrderJob` are not involved at all for sandbox orders, since there's no real network latency to hide from the admin request, and it means a sandbox order never depends on a queue worker actually running (a real, documented gotcha that already bit a live session this week per `prd.md`'s Price Sync founder-testing note). The admin chooses the simulated outcome (success, or failure with a canned error code/message) each time via an extra control in the reused Resend Delivery modal, visible only in the sandbox context — a fake adapter that only ever "succeeds" would make it impossible to test the exact `need_action` → `Resend Delivery` → outcome loop this tool exists to exercise.
6. **One new, narrow guard in existing fulfillment code — the only touch to money-critical logic this ADR makes:** `OrderFulfillmentService::creditProfit()` gets `if ($order->is_test) { return; }` before it writes any `LedgerEntry`. This is deliberately the single, explicit, easy-to-audit place a sandbox order is stopped from ever reaching the real ledger — chosen over a parallel "sandbox fulfillment service" specifically so the real status-transition/reference-number logic stays 100% shared and unduplicated between real and test orders (only the money-writing tail end is skipped), and chosen over swapping `LedgerService` itself (a `final` class, not behind an interface — substituting it would be a much larger change for the same guarantee).
7. **Cleanup is a real delete action in the sandbox page itself** (single row, and a "Delete All Test Orders" bulk action) — hard-deletes the `Order` row; `order_resend_attempts` cascade-deletes with it (existing FK). Safe with no residue precisely because of decision #6: a sandbox order, by construction, never had a real `LedgerEntry` to leave behind.
8. **Frontend: extract, don't duplicate.** The order-detail cards, the Resend Delivery modal, and the Delivery Logs table (already built for `/admin/orders`, ADR-017) are pulled into shared components consumed by **both** `/admin/orders` and the new `/middleware/sandbox` page, each against its own backend endpoint (`Admin\OrderController` vs. `Middleware\SandboxOrderController`). This is what actually delivers the founder's stated goal — "output yang sama macam workflow production" — without the two pages' behavior silently drifting apart over time the way two independently-maintained UIs would.

**Rationale:** Every decision above keeps `PricingService`, `OrderStatusService`, `OrderResendService`'s validation logic, and the `order_resend_attempts` audit trail completely unchanged and shared — the only new, sandbox-specific code is the `is_test` scope, the `FakeSupplierAdapter`, one guard line in `creditProfit()`, and the dedicated controller/page. This is the same "deepen the module, don't reshape the seam" discipline `ADR-001`/`ADR-006`/`ADR-014`/`ADR-017` already established, applied to a testing concern instead of a business feature — and it's the concrete difference between this design and the legacy page it was prompted by: isolation enforced at the query/ledger boundary, not left as an unenforced label.

**Consequence to track:** this ADR records *design intent only* — no code exists yet, matching this project's own established practice (`ADR-013`/`ADR-015`/`ADR-016`/`ADR-017`). Update `prd.md` §14/§15 once this actually ships. Decision #5's exact `FakeSupplierAdapter` outcome-picker UI and decision #8's exact shared-component boundaries are implementation details to finalize during the build session, not decisions still open — the founder-facing behavior (mock delivery, admin picks the outcome, fully separate page, real delete) is what's confirmed here.

## ADR-019: Second-pass resilience & security audit — reconciling ADR-014 against real code, docs restructure

**Status:** Accepted — 2026-07-27 (findings and sequencing discussed with the founder in a dedicated audit session; grilled on the "fix now vs. wait for deploy" split specifically, not per-item)

**Context:** ADR-014 (2026-07-26) recorded a 24/7 burst-resilience baseline — queue, retry, indexing, caching, rate-limiting, observability — as design intent, later confirmed built the same day (`prd.md` §14, 2026-07-26 entry). A full read-only re-audit was run 2026-07-27 (four scoped reviews: DB indexing + caching, queue/retry/load-balancing, observability, and OWASP-adjacent security — mass assignment, validation, CSRF, XSS, SQL injection) to verify ADR-014 against the actual code rather than trust the design doc, and to check the security surface ADR-014 didn't scope at all.

Result: all six of ADR-014's decisions are genuinely shipped as designed. Two things that looked like gaps on first read are not — they're the founder's own already-recorded deferrals: Redis (ADR-014 decision #1, deferred until real traffic justifies the infra) and Sentry/external error-tracking (ADR-014 decision #6, explicitly declined for cost/data-residency before real production traffic exists). What the audit did find genuinely new: a handful of code-level gaps ADR-014 never scoped (mostly on the auth/payment edges), one correction to an existing docs claim, and a confirmation that the project's production-infra gap (no queue worker, no Redis/S3 provisioned anywhere — `docker-compose.yml` still defines MySQL only) is real and unaddressed, consistent with `prd.md`'s own repeated note that this project is still 100% local Herd, no production host chosen (ADR-010).

**Decision — sequenced by what's actionable now vs. genuinely blocked on a production-host decision, not by raw severity:**

1. **Fix now — pure code/migration, no infra dependency, testable on local Herd:**
   - Add an index on `orders.created_at` (the default, unfiltered Admin Orders listing sorts by it with nothing backing that sort) and replace the "today" filter's `whereDate('created_at', ...)` with `whereBetween()` — `whereDate()` wraps the column in a function, which defeats any index on it regardless.
   - Verify the 7 tables using `foreignId()->constrained()` without a confirmed standalone index (`player_region_mappings`, `player_validations`, `price_change_logs`, `deactivation_logs`, `order_resend_attempts`, `games.player_validator_profile_id`, `gallery_images.uploaded_by`) via `SHOW INDEX` against real MySQL — the same gotcha already hit and fixed once, on `packages.supplier_id` (see ADR-006's neighboring migration note).
   - Add an idempotency key to `XenditGateway::createPayment()` — the shared `TransientFailureRetryPolicy` (ADR-014 #2) can retry a request that Xendit actually processed but whose response was lost, creating a second live payment request for the same order. This is a real double-charge risk distinct from order-fulfillment idempotency (PAY-2), which is already handled.
   - Add the same explicit short HTTP timeout to `XenditGateway::client()` that `GamevionAdapter` already has (with its own documented reasoning) — without it, a slow Xendit response can hold a request thread for the HTTP client's much longer default, compounded across retry attempts, on what is a customer-facing checkout path.
   - Log checkout failures (`CheckoutController`'s `catch (CheckoutFailedException $e)`, currently silent — no record anywhere of *why* a checkout failed) and admin login attempts, success and failure (`AuthController::login()`, currently unlogged — no audit trail for a brute-force attempt or a compromised account).
   - Rate-limit `POST /api/login` — the only mutating auth-adjacent route with no `throttle`, unlike `/checkout` (ADR-014 #4) and `/validate-player`.
   - Decide and either enforce or explicitly descope the existing `mfa_secret`/`mfa_enabled` columns on `AdminUser` — the schema exists (added ahead of this feature being built) but `AuthController::login()` never checks either, despite `foundation-security.md` mandating MFA ahead of withdrawal/voucher actions.
   - Fix `Admin\GalleryImageController` to read the upload disk from config (`FILESYSTEM_DISK`) instead of the hardcoded `'public'` string. This corrects `prd.md` §15's Image Gallery note ("a later swap to a real bucket costs a disk-config change, not a rewrite") — that's only true once this lands; today the disk is hardcoded, so an env-only swap wouldn't actually take effect.
2. **Defer until a production host is chosen — Redis/S3/worker specifics genuinely depend on the target, config now would be guesswork:**
   - Provision a real queue-worker process. `docker-compose.yml` defines `mysql` only — no worker container, no app container at all. This isn't hypothetical: the founder's own 2026-07-27 live-testing pass (`prd.md` §14) already hit the local-equivalent of this exact gap — Herd doesn't run a worker on its own either.
   - Move `CACHE_STORE`/`QUEUE_CONNECTION` off `database` to Redis once there's ops budget for the extra infra — reaffirming, not overriding, ADR-014 decision #1's own deferral reasoning.
   - Move gallery/hero-slide uploads to the already-configured (but unused) `s3` filesystem disk once a bucket exists — blocked on item 1's disk-config fix first.
   - Wire centralized log shipping — a Papertrail-shaped channel template already exists in `config/logging.php`, unused — once there's a production target to ship to.
3. **Revisit once there's real production traffic to learn from:**
   - Thread a request-correlation ID from inbound HTTP requests into the jobs they dispatch (each job already logs with good internal context via `Log::withContext()`; there's just no link from "this customer's request" to "the job it triggered" today).
   - Basic metrics — queue depth, job failure rate, checkout error rate. Extend `HealthController` with a threshold check first; a full metrics exporter is a later, bigger lift.
   - Schedule the existing `Smoke\{Xendit,Gamevion}SmokeTest` console commands as synthetic monitoring instead of leaving them dev/manual-only.
   - Add client-side error tracking to `admin/` and `storefront/` (neither has an `error.tsx` boundary or a reporting client today — a crashed component or failed fetch on the storefront is currently invisible until a customer complains).
   - FRAUD-1..4 (blacklist) — already tracked "Not started" in `prd.md` §15, reaffirmed here as a real, stated requirement in `foundation-security.md` with zero implementation, not a silent gap.
   - The small `lockForUpdate()` gap in `Admin\WithdrawalController::reject()`/`complete()` (unlike `approve()`, which already locks) — an audit-trail race only, no double financial movement, since the ledger is only touched in `approve()`.
4. **Docs restructure, done alongside this ADR:** root `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` were auto-generated multi-agent-swarm tooling boilerplate with zero project-specific content — confirmed unused in practice (this audit session used none of it). Replaced with project-specific orientation (stack, layout, working conventions, ADR-driven-decision discipline) in `AGENTS.md`, with `CLAUDE.md` now a one-line `@AGENTS.md` import, matching the pattern `admin/`/`storefront/` already used. Added `backend/CLAUDE.md` (Laravel-specific conventions, loaded only when working in `backend/`, per how nested `CLAUDE.md` files are actually resolved) and a root `README.md` for onboarding/handoff. `mattpocock-skills` (grilling, codebase-design, domain-modeling) are named explicitly in `AGENTS.md` as the project's house style, since their vocabulary was already showing up unattributed in this very ADR log (`ADR-014`'s "each grilled with the founder," this doc's repeated "deepen the module, don't reshape the seam") — making the practice explicit rather than leaving it implicit.

**Rationale:** Same interface-vs-implementation discipline as every prior resilience/security ADR — nothing in Decision-1 or Decision-2 changes a public contract (`PaymentGateway`, `SupplierAdapter`, `OrderFulfillmentService` are all untouched). Sequencing by deploy-dependency rather than raw severity matches this project's actual state: the code-level fixes cost nothing to do now and mean deploy day is infra wiring only, not a second security pass rushed under launch pressure; the infra-dependent items would just be guesswork before a host is chosen, and revisiting them then is not a delay, it's the correct order of operations.

**Consequence to track:** update `prd.md` §14/§15 as each Decision-1 item ships — this is exactly the kind of finding `AGENTS.md`'s new "keep §14/§15 current" convention exists for. Decisions 2 and 3 are sequencing intent, not scope reduction — each has an explicit trigger condition (production host chosen / real traffic exists) to re-open it; don't let "deferred" quietly become "forgotten." The full findings detail (file:line-level, all four scoped reviews) lives in the audit session transcript, not duplicated here — this entry records the decisions made from it, per this doc's own established convention (see ADR-014's Context for the same choice).

**Addendum — self-review before committing this session's docs changes, 2026-07-27 (same session, not a new audit round):**

1. **Missed finding: per-supplier circuit breaker.** `foundation-security.md` §6 and `prd.md` (DASH-2, §9 Non-Functional Requirements) both state this as an explicit **MVP** requirement — unchecked in the checklist, not implemented in code, and this ADR's Decision-1/2/3 lists above do not cover it. What exists today (`TransientFailureRetryPolicy`) is a different mechanism: it retries *within* one request; a circuit breaker trips *across* requests after repeated failures and stops attempting calls to a down supplier for a cooldown window, preventing a retry storm across many concurrent orders when a supplier has a sustained outage. This is pure code with no infra dependency (belongs conceptually with Decision-1), but is a larger unit of work than that list's other items (a new stateful component, not a one-line fix or single migration) — recorded here as its own explicitly tracked item rather than silently folded into either list: **build a `SupplierCircuitBreaker` (or equivalent) wrapping the `GamevionAdapter`/`XenditGateway` call sites, before treating ADR-019's fix-now list as complete.**
2. **This entry's own "Accepted" status overstated how thoroughly the individual decisions were reviewed.** Unlike ADR-014/015/016/017/018, each of which records being "grilled with the founder one at a time," this session grilled the *fix-now vs. defer-until-host vs. defer-until-traffic sequencing* as one decision, not each of the roughly fifteen individual findings one by one. Recorded here rather than silently edited into the Status line above, per this project's own no-silent-rewrite convention (`foundation-security.md`'s own stated rule for itself, applied here to this doc too).

**Consequence to track:** the circuit breaker item is not yet reflected in `prd.md` §14/§15 — add it once built, same as any other Decision-1 item.
